settings.name_in_paper: Best-arm identification in linear bandits with fixed confidence ((epsilon,delta)-best-arm identification with epsilon=0)
unmapped: noise is zero-mean i.i.d. and bounded in [-sigma, sigma] (stronger than sub-Gaussian)
settings.definition_quote: Let $\X\subseteq \Re^d$ be a finite set of arms, where $|\X| = K$ and the $\ell_2$-norm of any arm $x\in\X$ ... is upper-bounded by $L$. ... $r(x) = x^\top \theta^* + \eps$, where $\eps$ is a zero-mean i.i.d. noise bounded in $[-\sigma;\sigma]$. ... we will focus on the case of $\epsilon=0$ and we will provide high-probability bounds on the sample complexity $n$.

symbols.beta_apx: approximation factor of the method used to compute the G-allocation (performance within (1+beta) of optimal)
symbols.log_n: log(c' n^2 K^2/delta) with c' = 6/pi^2, n the stopping time

source.label: thm:g.allocation
source.quote: If the $G$-allocation strategy is implemented with a $\beta$-approximate method and the stopping condition in Eq.~\ref{eq:emp.stop.condition.2} is used, then $\Prob\bigg[ N^G \leq \frac{16c^2 d (1+\beta)\log_n(K^2/\delta)}{\Delta_{\min}^2} \wedge \Pi(\htheta_{N^G}) = x^* \bigg] \geq 1-\delta.$

results.notes: Bound holds jointly with correct identification w.p. >= 1-delta. The log term depends on n (the stopping time) itself, so the bound is implicit. Compute marked polynomial since approximate implementations (convex relaxation + rounding, greedy) are polynomial, though exact discrete design is NP-hard.

symbols.beta_apx: approximation factor of the method used to compute the XY-allocation
symbols.log_n: log(c' n^2 K^2/delta) with c' = 6/pi^2, n the stopping time

source.label: thm:xy.allocation
source.quote: If the $\X\Y$-allocation strategy is implemented with a $\beta$-approximate method and the stopping condition in Eq.~\ref{eq:emp.stop.condition.2} is used, then $\Prob\bigg[ N^{\X\Y} \leq \frac{32c^2 d (1+\beta)\log_n(K^2/\delta)}{\Delta_{\min}^2} \wedge \Pi(\htheta_{N^{\X\Y}}) = x^* \bigg] \geq 1-\delta.$

results.notes: Joint with correct identification w.p. >= 1-delta. Log term implicit in n.

symbols.beta_apx: approximation factor of the allocation method
symbols.M_star: number of steps needed by static XY-allocation to discard all suboptimal directions (Eq. m.value)
symbols.N_star: oracle sample complexity c^2 H_LB log_n(K^2/delta), H_LB = min_lambda max_{y in Y*} ||y||^2_{Lambda_lambda^{-1}}/Delta^2(y)

source.label: thm:xy.adaptive
source.quote: If the $\X\Y$-Adaptive allocation strategy is implemented with a $\beta$-approximate method and the stopping condition in Eq.~\ref{eq:emp.stop.condition.2} is used, then $\Prob\bigg[ N \leq \frac{(1+\beta)\max\{M^*,\frac{16}{\alpha}N^*\}}{\log(1/\alpha)} \log\Big(\frac{c\sqrt{\log_n(K^2/\delta)}}{\Delta_{\min}}\Big) \wedge \Pi(\htheta_{N}) = x^* \bigg] \geq 1-\delta.$

results.notes: Joint with correct identification w.p. >= 1-delta. M* and N* are problem-dependent quantities defined in the paper.
